To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a genome-wide RNA interference screen identified 64 genes required for the DNA damage response in the G2 phase of mitosis, and that in vivo analysis of two of these genes, mus101 (encoding a component of the replication preinitation complex) and mus312 (encoding a subunit of the nuclease complex involved in DSB repair), revealed their previously unappreciated role in the G2 DNA damage checkpoint.
we have identified a set of genes required for the G 2 - M checkpoint in Drosophil a cells and we have identified two novel genes that play important roles in the G 2-M checkpoint in Drosopila cells.
we identified 64 genes required for the Drosophila G2-M checkpoint using genome-wide RNAi screening, and that the G2-M checkpoints in Drosophilla and mammals share many components and mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the cell senses DNA damage and responds by activating cell cycle arrest.
the molecular mechanisms that control the DNA damage checkpoint.
the mechanisms by which the cell responds to DNA damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the G2-M Checkpoint, a mechanism by which DNA damage is sensed and transmitted to the cell cycle, is an evolutionarily conserved pathway that is essential for cell survival and organismal development.
the G2-M cell cycle checkpoint is a complex network of pathways that coordinate the cell cycle and repair processes to maintain genome integrity.
the G2-M Checkpoint is an important and complex mechanism for the cell to cope with DNA Damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a number of new genes that are involved in the G2/M checkpoint, and that we have shown that two genes that were already known to be important for DNA repair are also important for the G-2/M checkpoint.
we performed the largest RNAi screen in Drosopila to date and found 64 genes that are required for the G-2 M checkpoint.
the G2-M cell cycle checkpoint is a complex process that involves a large number of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a genome-wide RNA interference (RNAi) screen can identify genes that function in a particular pathway in the context of a specific stimulus.
a genome-wide RNA interference (RNAi) screen is a useful method to identify genes and pathways that are important for the DNA damage response.
the G2-M cell cycle checkpoint, a mechanism that is activated in response to damage to the genome, is an evolutionarily conserved mechanism that has been conserved in all eukaryotes.
